description: W0 evidence manifest for one release candidate: immutably binds the candidate source SHA and source-tree digest, package inputs, referenced schema versions, test suites and run IDs, scientific run IDs, artifacts with SHA-256 digests, and gate verdicts by reference to the verify_release.py JSON output. Gate verdicts are status strings only; full gate results live in the referenced output file and are never duplicated here. See docs/verification/evidence-manifest-spec.md.

artifacts.description: Every artifact that belongs to this candidate, each bound by its SHA-256 over persisted bytes. Paths are relative to the candidate root.

role.description: What the artifact is for the candidate (for example wheel, sdist, sbom, provenance, notes, checksums, report). Free-form so future asset types are not blocked; verify_release.py must reject an empty role.

candidate_source_sha.description: Full 40-hex Git SHA of the candidate commit. The manifest is bound to this exact commit; any other tree is a different candidate.

gate_results.description: Gate verdicts by reference. `gates` carries one status string per gate id; the full results (counts, logs, per-test outcomes) live ONLY in the referenced verify_release.py JSON output. Required gates accept ONLY `pass`.

detail.description: Optional one-line pointer or note (for example the section of the referenced output that records this gate). Must not duplicate gate results.

status.description: Exact gate-status vocabulary (frozen by W0): pass, fail, skipped, unavailable, not_applicable, zero_work. No other string is valid.

required_gates.description: Gate ids that must pass for this candidate to be promotable. The manifest verifier (W10 candidate dossier) and, at the CI level, the exact-SHA promotion gate enforce that every id listed here is present in gates with status pass; any other status blocks promotion. The list itself is part of the manifest so a candidate cannot silently drop a required gate.

verify_release_output.description: Pointer to the verify_release.py JSON output file for this candidate, bound by its SHA-256 over persisted bytes. The manifest never embeds that output.

manifest_version.description: Manifest format version. A future format change requires a new schema id (textforensics.evidence-manifest/v2); this field never silently changes meaning.

package_inputs.description: Package inputs that produced this candidate: the project itself plus every resolved dependency. Digest is the SHA-256 of the exact distribution artifact or lockfile entry the build consumed, as recorded by verify_release.py; it is not a hash of the package name.

recorded_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp (ISO 8601) when this manifest was written. Informational only; it is not part of any digest preimage.

schema_versions.description: Schema versions referenced by this candidate, as a map from schema name to its schema id (for example {"case-file": "textforensics.case-file/v1"}). At least one entry is required.

scientific_run_ids.description: Scientific run IDs (benchmark / validation / drift runs) that support this candidate. May be empty for a candidate with no scientific claims; the field itself is always present so absence is explicit, not omitted.

source_tree_digest.description: Digest of the candidate source tree, computed over persisted bytes. Method names the procedure so a verifier can reproduce it exactly.

method.description: Digest procedure. `git-tree` is the Git tree SHA of the candidate commit; `sha256-manifest` is a SHA-256 over a sorted manifest of (path, SHA-256) pairs for every tracked file. verify_release.py defines and implements the method it records.

value.description: Digest value: 40 hex for `git-tree`, 64 hex for `sha256-manifest`.

test_suites.description: Test suites executed for this candidate, each with its run ID. At least one suite is required: a candidate with zero executed test work is `zero_work`, never a pass.

run_id.description: Run identifier (CI run id, or a local run identifier recorded by verify_release.py).

suite.description: Suite name (for example core, extras, api, mcp, claims, mutation-diff).

title: TextForensics Evidence Manifest
